extracted.intended_audience: theatre practitioners, playwrights, critics, and students of comedy theory
extracted.subtask_description: Analytical framework for producing and evaluating comedic effect (especially theatrical/vaudeville comedy) by identifying mechanisms (repetition, inversion, puppet-like manipulation, cumulative chains, rhythm, suggestion) that turn the living into the mechanical and produce laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm of speech as source of comic singularity
rubrics_metrics.description: La singularité comique tient souvent au rythme de la parole (ex.: l’un scandant son discours syllabe par syllabe pendant que l’autre bredouille).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasts of vocal timing and tempo to create a physical/comic signature for a character; actors will instinctively compose such defects. Examples: contrasting an intoned speaker with a stammerer; rhythm can imply a bodily peculiarity that complements professional ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person perceived as thing (transfiguration into a thing)
rubrics_metrics.description: « Nous rions toutes les fois qu'une personne nous donne l'impression d'une chose. »
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create scenes where a human appears like a thing (Sancho Pança as a balloon, Baron Münchausen as a cannonball, clowns rebounding like rubber balls). Can be achieved by attitudes, movements, gambades, crescendo of mechanical action. The comic effect can arise even if the identification with a thing is partial—it suffices to suggest the direction (confusion of person and function).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual suggestion (from vague to distinct) as comic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Le passage graduel du confus au distinct est le procédé de suggestion par excellence; on prépare l'imagination par insinuation graduelle jusqu'à la forme précise de l'objet suggéré.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use progressive clarification—start with formless impressions and, degree by degree, make the image more precise so the audience 'sees' the hallucinated object. Examples: clowns whose movements first suggest packages, then balls; hypnotic analogy; poetic devices (rhythm, rime, assonance) that lull imagination into accepting the suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of a comic expression (force of suggestion)
rubrics_metrics.description: L'art du conteur/vaudevilliste ne consiste pas seulement à composer le mot; le difficile est de donner au mot sa force de suggestion en le rendant acceptable (il doit paraître sortir d’un état d’âme ou s’encadrer dans les circonstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comic formulations arise naturally from character emotions or circumstances. A phrase becomes comic when it fits the speaker’s state (e.g., M. Perrichon counting his parcels) or the situational frame; otherwise the device will feel forced and lose effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of comic situation
rubrics_metrics.description: « Est comique tout arrangement d'actes et d'événements qui nous donne, insérés l'un dans l'autre, l'illusion de la vie et la sensation d'un arrangement mécanique. »
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct situations that simultaneously evoke living continuity and an underlying mechanical arrangement—the tension between life and mechanization is the source of vaudeville comedy. Use simplification and magnification (as in theatre) to make these mechanisms visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diable à ressort (spring toy) — oscillation/repetition mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Le type du 'diable à ressort' : une force qui part comme un ressort, qu'on comprime et qui repart, produisant une répétition et crescendo comiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternating obstinacy (one force expressed, another resisting) to create a rhythmic repetition that escalates. Examples: repetitive hitting and rebound of characters, the doctor scolding Argan whose attempts to silence the doctor only make him return with a new malediction. The device evolves from a material to a moral mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition as comic device (word and situation)
rubrics_metrics.description: La répétition n'est pas risible par elle-même; elle devient comique parce qu'elle symbolise un jeu moral/matériel : il y a généralement deux termes en présence — un sentiment qui se détend comme un ressort et une idée qui le comprime de nouveau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using repetition, ensure it signals an underlying automaticity or fixed impulse (e.g., Dorine/Orgon, Harpagon's 'sans dot !'). Repetition should make visible a mechanism (habit, obsession) or internal conflict, not be an isolated gimmick.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pantin à ficelles (puppet-on-strings) — manipulation device
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnage qui paraît agir librement mais, vu d’un certain côté, apparaît comme un simple jouet entre les mains d’un autre; le pantin à ficelles transforme la liberté apparente en mécanisme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatize characters controlled by others (Scapin manipulating Géronte/Argante) or by internal opposing parts; personify opposing wills so the puppet's motion is understood. The spectator often sympathizes with the manipulators; ensure the 'strings' are perceptible via action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boule de neige (cumulative chain) — propagation and acceleration
rubrics_metrics.description: Le dispositif de la boule de neige : un effet se propage en s’ajoutant à lui-même, la petite cause aboutissant à un grand effet, souvent accélérant jusqu'à la catastrophe; il est souvent réversible/circulaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build scenes where a trivial incident triggers a chain of increasingly grave/unexpected events (letters lost, a hat chased through Paris). The structure may be rectilinear or circular (returning the characters to the point of departure), and should feel natural while amplifying consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three fundamental procedures: répétition, inversion, interférence des séries
rubrics_metrics.description: Les trois procédés essentiels du vaudeville/comique sont la répétition, l'inversion et l'interférence des séries — découlant des caractères du vivant (progression temporelle, irréversibilité, indivisibilité spatiale) et leur contrepied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When devising comic material, think in terms of these three meta-procedures: repeat a situation; invert expected temporal/causal order; create interfering series of events that cross and produce mechanical-looking outcomes. These procedures, mixed in variable doses, generate most comic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast living vs mechanical as criterion for comic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Le comique naît quand on surprend du mécanisme (raideur, automatisme) dans la continuité vivante des êtres; la vie est normalement progrès continu, irréversibilité et individualité — le comique montre leur contre-image mécanique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design comic scenes to reveal moments when attention lapses, habits, or mechanized responses make people resemble things; laughter acts as a social corrective. The stronger and clearer the perceived mechanization within living action, the stronger the comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition of complex situations (not just words) is especially comic
rubrics_metrics.description: La répétition d'une situation (une combinaison d'éléments) qui revient plusieurs fois, insérée dans une série progressive, produit une coïncidence comique d'autant plus forte que la scène répétée est plus complexe et amenée naturellement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure multi-act returns of a scene/encounter so that a complex incident recurs plausibly—this is commonly used in vaudeville (same encounter across different milieus) to create humor through recurrence of the mechanical pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience alignment and crafting sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Par instinct, le public se range souvent du côté des fourbes/manipulateurs plutôt que des dupes (ex.: l'enfant prend le parti du dupeur qui manœuvre la poupée).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating manipulative characters or schemes, anticipate audience sympathy for the clever manipulator; craft the manipulation to be playful rather than cruel so spectators enjoy being complicit.
